name: Hot & Sour Soup Chicken
description: A tangy, peppery Indo-Chinese soup with shredded chicken and vegetables simmered in a light, cornstarch-thickened broth with vinegar. Its balance of heat and sourness makes it a popular starter at Indian-Chinese restaurants.

name: Attukal Soup
description: A rich, slow-simmered mutton bone-marrow soup prized for its deep, gelatinous broth. It's traditionally spiced with pepper and warming spices and served as a hearty South Indian starter.

name: Bread Basket
description: An assortment platter of Plain Naan, Butter Naan, Garlic Naan, and Parotta, letting guests sample the restaurant's tandoor breads together. A great shareable starter for the table.

name: Pulav Rice (Weekends)
description: Basmati rice gently cooked with whole spices, ghee, and aromatics using the single-pot pulao method, giving it a light, evenly infused flavor. A mildly spiced weekend rice special.

name: Tandoori Fish (Whole Fish) Weekends
description: A whole fish marinated in yogurt and tandoori spices, then roasted in a clay tandoor for a smoky, charred finish. A weekend seafood special.

name: Veg Corn Soup
description: A comforting, lightly thickened soup made with sweet corn kernels and mixed vegetables in a mild broth. A popular vegetarian starter in Indo-Chinese style Indian restaurants.

name: Hariyali Paneer Kebab
description: Cubes of paneer marinated in a vibrant green paste of mint, coriander, and green chillies, then grilled in the tandoor. A fragrant, herbaceous vegetarian kebab.

name: Curd Rice
description: Cooked rice mixed with fresh yogurt and tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chillies. A cooling, mild South Indian comfort dish often eaten at the end of a meal.

name: Puri (3)+Goat Kheema Curry (12 oz)
description: Three golden, puffed puris served with a 12 oz portion of minced goat (kheema) curry simmered in an onion-tomato masala. A hearty North Indian-style breakfast or meal combo.

name: Puri (3)+Chicken Curry (12 oz)
description: Three crispy, puffed puris paired with a 12 oz portion of chicken curry in a spiced onion-tomato gravy. A satisfying combo popular for breakfast or a quick meal.

name: Onion Mirchi Bajji
description: Sliced onions and green chillies dipped in spiced gram-flour batter and deep-fried until crisp. A popular South Indian tea-time snack with a spicy kick.

name: Chilli Bullet Naan
description: Tandoor-baked naan bread topped with chopped green chillies for an extra spicy kick. It pairs well with rich, creamy curries to balance the heat.

name: Garlic Naan
description: Soft, pillowy tandoor-baked flatbread brushed with butter and topped with fresh chopped garlic. A classic accompaniment for curries and kebabs.

name: Onion Samosa
description: A crisp, deep-fried pastry shell filled with spiced onions instead of the usual potato filling. Served as a savory tea-time snack, often with chutney.

name: Avakai Rice
description: Steamed rice mixed with tangy, fiery Andhra avakaya (raw mango pickle) made with mustard seed and red chilli. A bold, pickle-forward rice dish popular in Telugu households.

name: Malai Chicken Kebab (Boneless)
description: Boneless chicken marinated in a rich, creamy mixture of cream, cheese, and mild spices, then grilled in the tandoor. Known for its melt-in-the-mouth texture and delicate flavor.

name: Chole Bhature
description: A North Indian classic pairing spicy, tangy chickpea curry (chole) with fluffy, deep-fried bhature bread. One of Delhi's most iconic street-food combinations.

name: Tandoori Chicken
description: Chicken marinated in yogurt and a blend of tandoori spices, then roasted in a clay tandoor for a smoky, charred, and juicy result. One of India's most iconic dishes.

name: Plain Naan
description: A classic leavened Indian flatbread made from refined flour dough, baked in a tandoor until soft and lightly charred. Served as an everyday accompaniment to curries.

name: Dum Rice
description: Basmati rice slow-cooked with spices using the sealed dum method for deeply infused flavor and fluffy, separate grains. A fragrant, mildly spiced rice dish.

name: Onion Pakora
description: Thinly sliced onions coated in spiced chickpea-flour batter and deep-fried into crispy fritters. A classic Indian tea-time snack.

name: Veg Samosa
description: A triangular, deep-fried pastry filled with spiced potatoes, peas, and herbs. One of India's most iconic savory snacks, usually served with tamarind or mint chutney.

name: Idli Sambar
description: Soft, steamed rice-and-lentil cakes served dunked in tangy, tamarind-based sambar. A classic South Indian breakfast staple.

name: Sambar Rice Veg
description: Rice mixed with tangy, tamarind-based sambar lentil stew and vegetables, served with crisp fryums. A comforting South Indian one-bowl meal.

name: Puri (3)+Goat Curry (12 oz)
description: Three fried, puffed puris served alongside a 12 oz portion of tender goat meat curry in a robust spiced gravy. A filling combo meal in North Indian dhaba style.

name: Sambar Rice Chicken
description: Rice combined with tangy sambar lentil stew and tender chicken, served with crisp fryums. A hearty non-vegetarian twist on the South Indian classic.

name: Puri (3)+Chole (12 oz)
description: Three puffed puris paired with a 12 oz portion of spicy chickpea (chole) curry. A vegetarian take on the classic chole-and-bread combination.

name: Tomato Soup
description: A smooth, tangy tomato-based soup, lightly spiced and often finished with a touch of cream. A classic mild starter found on most Indian restaurant menus.

name: Gongura Rice
description: Steamed rice tossed with tangy, tart gongura (sorrel leaf) chutney, a Telugu specialty known for its distinctive sour flavor. A signature Andhra rice preparation.

name: Hariyali Chicken Kebab
description: Chicken pieces marinated in a vibrant green mint-coriander-chilli paste and grilled in the tandoor. Known for its fresh, herby flavor and moist texture.

name: White Rice
description: Plain steamed rice served as a neutral base to pair with any curry. A simple staple accompaniment.

name: Hot & Sour Soup Veg
description: The vegetarian version of the classic Indo-Chinese hot and sour soup, made with mixed vegetables, vinegar, and white pepper in a light, thickened broth. It delivers the same tangy, spicy balance without any meat.

name: Cut Mirchi Bajji
description: Long green chillies split, stuffed with spiced filling, and dipped in gram-flour batter before deep-frying. A fiery South Indian snack, often served with chutney.

name: Chicken Corn Soup
description: A mild, comforting soup combining shredded chicken and sweet corn in a light, slightly thickened broth. A popular starter blending Chinese-style technique with Indian seasoning.

name: Parotta (Kerala Style)
description: A flaky, layered flatbread made by folding and pan-frying dough with oil, giving it a crisp, laminated texture similar to a croissant. A Kerala-style staple usually paired with spicy curries.

name: Mirchi Bajji
description: Whole green chillies dipped in spiced gram-flour batter and deep-fried into crunchy fritters. A beloved spicy South Indian street snack.

name: Idli (4)
description: Four soft, steamed cakes made from a fermented rice-and-urad-dal batter. A light, healthy South Indian breakfast staple, usually served with chutney and sambar.

name: Sambar Lentil Soup
description: A tangy, tamarind-based South Indian lentil soup cooked with toor dal, vegetables, and a tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves. Served here as a warming starter.

name: Butter Naan
description: Tandoor-baked naan bread finished with a generous brushing of melted butter for a rich, soft finish. A popular classic alongside any curry.

name: Chicken Tikka Kebab
description: Boneless chicken marinated in yogurt and warm spices, then char-grilled in a tandoor until smoky and slightly crisp at the edges. A staple tandoori appetizer worldwide.

name: Veg Pakora
description: An assortment of mixed vegetables coated in spiced chickpea-flour batter and deep-fried until golden and crisp. A classic Indian tea-time fritter.

name: Puri (3)+Bhaji (12 oz)
description: Three crisp puris served with a 12 oz portion of spiced mixed-vegetable bhaji curry. A comforting vegetarian breakfast combo.

name: Chicken Masakali
description: Chicken tossed in a seasoned salt blend with the house Masakali masala and curry leaves for a distinctively spiced, tangy appetizer. Choose your preferred spice level from mild to hot.

name: Curry Leaf Veg
description: Vegetables sautéed with crushed pepper, onions, and green chillies, finished with fresh curry leaves. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer for a peppery, aromatic starter.

name: Potlam Parotta (Chicken)
description: Flaky parotta bread served alongside a rich chicken curry, presented in the 'potlam' style reminiscent of banana-leaf-wrapped biryani packets. A hearty combo meal.

name: Kottu Parotta Chicken
description: Shredded parotta stir-fried on a hot griddle with chicken, egg, and spices — a beloved South Indian/Sri Lankan street-food technique. Known for its rich, buttery, well-seasoned bite.

name: Rayalaseema Kodi Vepudu
description: A fiery Rayalaseema-style dry chicken fry, roasted with bone-in pieces in a bold chilli-spice paste until each bite develops a crackling, spice-crusted exterior. Known for the intense heat characteristic of the Rayalaseema region.

name: Regular Fried Rice
description: Wok-tossed rice stir-fried with vegetables and a choice of protein (veg, paneer, egg, chicken, or shrimp) in light Indo-Chinese seasoning. A classic Indian-Chinese staple.

name: Chef Mani's Special Chicken
description: The head chef's signature preparation, made with dried red chillies, coriander seeds, and dried garlic for a deeply aromatic, spiced chicken dish.

name: Menta Chicken
description: Chicken cooked in a distinctive sauce made with fresh mint, yogurt, and warming spices for a cooling yet flavorful appetizer.

name: Street Style Noodles
description: Stir-fried noodles tossed with vegetables and a choice of protein in bold, street-cart-style seasoning. Inspired by Indian roadside Chinese food stalls.

name: Idli (3) + Mutton Curry (12oz)
description: Three soft steamed idlis paired with a 12 oz portion of rich, spiced mutton curry. An unconventional but hearty non-vegetarian breakfast or meal combo.

name: Majestic Veg
description: Vegetables deep-fried and tossed in a vibrant yellow house-special sauce. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer for a tangy, mildly spiced appetizer.

name: Kottu Parotta Veg
description: Shredded parotta bread stir-fried with mixed vegetables and spices on a hot griddle. A vegetarian version of the popular kottu street-food dish.

name: Madurai Chicken Pakoda (B/L)
description: Boneless chicken deep-fried and tempered with curry leaves and spices, in the style of Madurai's famous street-food chicken pakoda. Known for its crisp texture and peppery finish.

name: Karampodi Veg
description: Deep-fried vegetables tossed in Andhra's fiery karam podi — a spice powder of red chillies, lentils, garlic, and tamarind. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer for a bold, textured bite.

name: Monagadi Vepudu
description: A fiery Andhra-style dry fry, deep-fried and tossed in a bold spicy sauce, with a choice of chicken, fish, or shrimp. Known for its crispy texture and intense heat.

name: Karampodi
description: Deep-fried protein tossed in Andhra's iconic karam podi spice powder of red chillies, lentils, garlic, and tamarind for a fiery, textured finish. Choice of chicken, fish, or shrimp.

name: Chicken 555
description: Deep-fried chicken sautéed in a special aromatic '555' sauce, a signature house preparation known for its bold, tangy-spicy flavor.

name: Parotta + Goat Curry (12oz)
description: Flaky, layered parotta bread served with a 12 oz portion of rich, slow-cooked goat curry. A classic South Indian combo meal.

name: Idli (3) + Chicken Curry (12oz)
description: Three soft steamed idlis served with a 12 oz portion of spiced chicken curry. A filling combination of South Indian breakfast staple and hearty gravy.

name: Chicken Momos
description: Steamed dumplings filled with spiced minced chicken, a Tibetan/Nepali-origin street food now hugely popular across India. Available steamed or finished tandoor-style.

name: Parotta + Chicken Curry (12oz)
description: Layered, flaky parotta bread paired with a 12 oz portion of spiced chicken curry. A satisfying combo popular across South India.

name: Mirapa Veg
description: Deep-fried vegetables tossed in a spicy green-chilli sauce for a vibrant vegetarian appetizer. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer.

name: Masala Fish Fry
description: Fish tempered with curry leaves and green chillies, then sautéed in a hot red sauce. A classic Andhra-style crispy fish appetizer.

name: Schezwan Fried Rice

name: Curry Leaf

name: Fresh Mint

name: Cashew

name: Cashew Chicken
description: Fried chicken cooked in a special savory sauce with roasted cashew nuts for a nutty, crunchy contrast to the spiced chicken.

description: Boneless goat meat pan-fried with onions, curry leaves, and crushed black pepper for a robust, peppery South Indian appetizer.

name: Chicken Manchurian
description: Deep-fried chicken sautéed in a glossy, tangy soy-based Manchurian sauce. A classic Indo-Chinese fusion dish loved for its bold umami flavor.

name: Schezwan Noodles
description: Stir-fried noodles tossed with vegetables and a choice of protein in spicy, garlicky schezwan sauce. A fiery favorite among Indo-Chinese noodle dishes.

name: Masakali
description: A vegetarian version of the house Masakali preparation, tossed in seasoned salt with signature masala and curry leaves. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer.

name: Regular Hakka Noodles
description: Stir-fried thin wheat noodles tossed with vegetables and a choice of protein in classic Indo-Chinese Hakka-style seasoning. A staple of Indian-Chinese cuisine.

name: Karam Royalla Vepudu
description: A fiery Rayalaseema-style pan-fried shrimp dish, tossed in a bold chilli-spice paste until crisp. Known for its intense heat and deep, roasted flavor.

name: Majestic
description: Deep-fried protein tossed in a vibrant yellow house-special sauce for a tangy, mildly spiced appetizer. Choice of chicken or fish.

name: Kottu Parotta Egg
description: Shredded parotta stir-fried with egg and spices on a hot griddle. A protein-rich twist on the classic kottu preparation.

description: The vegetarian version of the head chef's signature preparation, made with dried red chillies, coriander seeds, and dried garlic. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer.

name: Masala Fried Rice
description: Wok-tossed rice stir-fried with vegetables, a choice of protein, and a robust blend of Indian masala spices. A flavorful twist on classic fried rice.

name: Crispy Masala Corn
description: Sweet corn kernels battered and deep-fried until crispy, then tossed in a spiced masala coating. A popular crunchy vegetarian starter.

name: Shrimp 65
description: Bite-sized deep-fried shrimp marinated in spiced batter and seasoned with curry leaves and red chilli, in the style of the classic Chicken 65. Known for its crispy texture and bold heat.

name: Veg 65
description: Bite-sized deep-fried vegetables marinated in a spiced batter and seasoned with curry leaves and red chilli, in the style of the classic Chicken 65. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer.

name: Karampodi Idli
description: Steamed idlis served with a choice of fiery karam podi (spice powder) — Guntur Chilli, Curry Leaf, or Gun Powder — for an extra punch of Andhra-style heat.

name: Chicken Lollipops
description: Chicken wings marinated in spices, coated in a zesty batter, and deep-fried until crisp. A popular finger-food appetizer resembling a drumstick lollipop.

name: Parotta + Goat Kheema Curry (12oz)
description: Flaky parotta bread served with a 12 oz portion of minced goat (kheema) curry cooked in a spiced onion-tomato base. A hearty combo meal.

name: Manchurian
description: Deep-fried vegetables sautéed in a glossy, tangy soy-based Manchurian sauce. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer for the classic Indo-Chinese flavor.

name: Ulavcharu Kodi Vepudu
description: Diced chicken pan-fried with sliced green chillies, curry leaves, and Andhra spices for a bold, aromatic dry-fry appetizer.

name: Chilli Veg

name: Paneer Momos
description: Steamed dumplings filled with spiced paneer, offering a vegetarian take on the popular Tibetan/Nepali street food. Available steamed or finished tandoor-style.

name: Veg 555
description: Deep-fried vegetables sautéed in the restaurant's signature aromatic '555' sauce. Choice of veg, gobi, baby corn, or paneer for a bold, tangy-spicy appetizer.

name: Monagadi

name: Mirapa
description: Deep-fried protein tossed in a special spicy green-chilli sauce for a vibrant, fiery appetizer. Choice of chicken, fish, or shrimp.

name: Apollo Fish
description: Deep-fried fish tempered with curry leaves and green chillies, then sautéed in a hot red sauce. A beloved Andhra-style crispy seafood appetizer.

name: Mirapa Idli
description: Steamed idlis served with a spicy green-chilli based Mirapa sauce for a fiery twist on the traditional South Indian breakfast staple.

name: Navaratan Korma

name: Paneer Karaikudi
description: Paneer simmered in a coconut-based curry prepared in the Chettinad style from the Karaikudi region of Tamil Nadu. Known for its bold, aromatic spice blend.

name: Dum Ka Kheema
description: Minced goat cooked slowly with onions, tomatoes, and special spices using the sealed dum method for deep, concentrated flavor.

name: Saag Paneer
description: Soft paneer cubes simmered in a smooth, spiced spinach (saag) gravy. A classic North Indian vegetarian favorite known for its earthy, mildly peppery flavor.

name: Chettinad Chicken Fry
description: Boneless chicken pan-fried with a special Chettinad masala blend of roasted spices from Tamil Nadu's Chettinad region. Known for its bold, peppery, deeply aromatic flavor.

name: Malai Kofta
description: Crisp fried vegetable-and-paneer dumplings (koftas) simmered in a rich, creamy cashew-tomato gravy. 'Malai' refers to the dish's signature cream-based sauce.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Soft paneer cubes cooked in a velvety, buttery tomato-and-onion based sauce. One of India's most popular creamy vegetarian curries.

name: Okra Masala

name: Veg Kheema Peas Masala

name: Kadai Paneer

name: Kaju Paneer

name: Spinach Dal

name: Channa Masala

name: Mangalore Curry
description: Veg or paneer simmered in a coconut-and-spice gravy inspired by the coastal flavors of Mangalore. Known for its aromatic, herb-forward sauce.

name: Tikka Masala

name: Dal Tadka

name: Chicken Mughlai

name: Afghani Paneer

name: Gongura Dal

name: Afghani Masala

name: Paneer Tikka Masala

description: A kid-friendly combo of crispy fried chicken pakoda paired with a sweet, chilled mango lassi drink.

name: Mango Lassi
description: A chilled, creamy yogurt-based drink blended with sweet mango pulp. A refreshing classic accompaniment to spicy Indian meals.

name: Rasmalai
description: Soft, flattened cheese (chenna) patties soaked in sweetened, thickened milk flavored with cardamom and saffron. A rich, creamy North Indian dessert.

name: Thums Up

name: Can Soda

name: Kheema Stuffed Dosa

name: Egg Dosa

name: Plain Dosa
description: A thin, crispy fermented rice-and-lentil crepe, the foundational South Indian breakfast staple, usually served with chutney and sambar.

name: Onion Dosa
description: A crispy dosa topped with finely chopped onions cooked into the batter for extra flavor and crunch.

name: Masala Dosa
description: A crispy dosa filled with a spiced, mildly tangy potato masala. One of South India's most iconic and popular dishes.

name: Chilli Paneer Cut Dosa

name: Podi Dosa

name: Guntur Chilli Dosa

name: Ghee Roast 70mm Dosa

name: Mixed Veg Utthappam

name: Shrimp Masala

name: Bhature

name: Chicken Chukka

name: Goat Curry
